subject: MSA supplement: term extension + capacity increase (clarify termination / escrow language)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA supplement: term extension + capacity increase (clarify termination / escrow language)

Hi Ellen,

Thanks again for the productive renewal conversation last week. Per our call, I've attached a draft supplement to the existing MSA that: (1) extends the term 12 months, (2) adds the requested capacity bump for Q3 (+150k tokens/day committed), and (3) includes a short exhibit listing the add-on GPUs/region routing.

Two items from your legal note I wanted to call out proactively so we can avoid back-and-forth:
- Termination: your team asked for a 30-day rollback right tied to usage thresholds. We can agree to a 30-day cure on material breach, but the rollback tied to dynamic usage would need clearer guardrails (we propose scoped metrics and a 90-day notice).
- Escrow / data return: Acme requested language that would trigger an escrow release on insolvency. We typically offer expedited data export and a certified deletion window; full escrow of model artifacts is not something our infra supports today without an addendum.

I've attached ACME_Renewal_Supplement_v1.docx and the OrderForm_Q2_2028.pdf with the capacity lines. Could you share Acme legal's redlines so we can route internally to Legal (Laura) and Infrastructure (Aditya) to validate feasibility?

Proposed next steps: if we get redlines by EOD Monday (4/23), we can present a consolidated counter by Wednesday 4/25 and aim for signature by end of the month.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: MSA supplement: term extension + capacity increase (clarify termination / escrow language)

Vanessa —

Appreciate the draft. Attaching Acme legal's redlines (see inline comments). High-level flags:
1) Term rollback: we asked for the ability to reduce committed capacity with 30 days notice if our usage stays 30% below committed levels for two consecutive months. This is a protection for our finance team.
2) Insolvency escrow: request is limited to customer configuration + account exports (not Redwood model artifacts).
3) SLA credits: want a caps clause if multiple incidents occur in the renewal year — propose a 10% credit cap.

Attaching redlines: ACME_Renewal_Supplement_v1_Redlined.docx. Please confirm your ability to accept the usage-based rollback or propose concrete metric thresholds.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
VP Procurement, Acme Corp
ellen@acme-corp.com

Subject: Fwd: Acme redlines — term rollback / escrow / SLA caps — need intake

Forwarding Acme's redlines. Quick notes from Legal:
- Usage rollback: legal is okay discussing a structured rollback but needs the metrics defined (e.g., rolling 60-day window, baseline calculation, minimum committed floor). Commercial should confirm what Acme considers acceptable minima.
- Escrow: they clarified it's account exports only — acceptable, but we should confirm retention/export format and costs for expedited export. Ops (Aditya), can you confirm export SLA & format (e.g., JSON/NDJSON + token logs) and any additional tooling/fees?
- SLA credit cap: legal is fine with a commercial cap (10%) if we can preserve carve-outs for force majeure and scheduled maintenance.

Advise: propose language that ties rollback to a simple metric the platform can measure and a minimum committed threshold (e.g., cannot reduce below 40% of current committed capacity). Also outline export runbook and cost estimate.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme redlines — term rollback / escrow / SLA caps — need intake

Laura / Vanessa —

Ops feedback on the three asks:
- Usage measurement: we can instrument a rolling 60-day average of daily committed tokens. That gives a stable metric. We can emit an automated notice when the rolling avg is <70% of committed for 60 days. Implementation effort: minimal — mostly config + dashboard + billing flag.
- Minimum floor: can't go below 50% of committed without a formal review (because capacity allocations affect pooling). We can add an automatic temporary throttle but a permanent capacity reduction needs 30-day notice + manual ops approval.
- Exports: we can deliver account exports (metadata + user prompts + usage logs) in NDJSON within 5 business days for standard requests; expedited (48 hours) is available as a paid service. We'll prepare a runbook and cost estimate.

I'll draft suggested language to capture the rolling 60-day average, 70% trigger to notify, and a 50% floor on reductions. Also propose adding a line item for the expedited export fee in OrderForm_Q2_2028.pdf.

—Aditya
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA supplement: term extension + capacity increase (clarify termination / escrow language)

Ellen —

Thanks for the redlines and the quick turnaround. After internal review here are the concessions we can make today:
1) Usage rollback: agree to Acme's ability to request a committed capacity reduction with 30 days' notice, provided the rolling 60-day average is <= 70% of committed and the new level does not fall below 50% of prior committed capacity. We will add automated alerts and a manual ops review step.
2) Escrow/export: we accept the limited escrow request for account exports (metadata + prompts + usage logs). Standard export delivery = 5 business days; expedited 48-hour delivery available as paid service (fee to be added to order form).
3) SLA credits: we can accept a 10% aggregate credit cap for the renewal year with standard carve-outs for scheduled maintenance and force majeure.

Updated attachments: ACME_Renewal_Supplement_v2.docx (applies the language above) and OrderForm_Q2_2028_v2.pdf (adds expedited export line item). Please review and send any final redlines by COB Monday (4/23). If agreeable, we'll prepare DocuSign for signature the following week.

Best,
Vanessa
